description: A lowpass filter built as two resonant stages in series, with its cutoff modulated by two audio inputs, one added to the cutoff and one multiplying it

params.text: Scales the cutoff control input before it is added to the cutoff knob
Sets how far the FM A input is added to the cutoff
Sets the cutoff frequency across the whole audible range
Sets how far the FM B input multiplies the cutoff
Scales the FM A control input before it is added to the FM A amount
Scales the FM B control input before it is added to the FM B amount
Sets the resonance of both filter stages, which are given different amounts so the filter dirties rather than screams
Scales the resonance control input before it is added to the resonance knob
Sets the gain into the filter: silence at the bottom, untouched in the centre, four times at the top
Mixes some of the second stage's feedback term back into the output, which puts low end back after a steep cut
Scales the drive control input before it is added to the drive knob
Scales the bass control input before it is added to the bass knob

inputs.text: Added to the cutoff knob through the cutoff CV knob, a tenth of the cutoff range per volt at full amount
Modulates the cutoff by addition, scaled by the FM A amount; it does nothing until a cable is here
Modulates the cutoff by multiplication, scaled by the FM B amount; it does nothing until a cable is here
Added to the FM A amount through its CV knob, a tenth per volt at full amount
Added to the FM B amount through its CV knob, a tenth per volt at full amount
Added to the resonance knob through its CV knob, a tenth per volt at full amount
Added to the drive knob through its CV knob, a tenth per volt at full amount
Added to the bass knob through its CV knob, a tenth per volt at full amount
The signal to be filtered; the channel count on this cable sets the module's polyphony

outputs.text: The filtered signal, with as many channels as the input

notes: the cutoff knob starts fully down, where the filter passes almost nothing, so turn it up before expecting sound
the cutoff is held between a hundredth and 0.95 of the Nyquist frequency however far the knobs and the modulation push it, so the filter cannot be driven into silence or out of range
the two FM inputs are read only while something is patched into them; with both empty the cutoff is the knob and its control input alone
